messages:
From: Olivia Barnes <obarnes@syntharahealth.com>

Date: Wed, 28 Apr 2027 08:32:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal + capacity expansion — throughput commitment questions

Hi Karthik,

Thanks again for the renewal overview last week. We’re moving forward with renewing our Dedicated Reserved pool and want to increase our committed capacity as part of the contract: add 6 A100-equivalent GPUs to our current pool for the 12-month term. The key ask from our infra team is a firm throughput baseline so we can plan traffic shaping across our ingestion pipeline:

- Baseline committed throughput: 12,000 tokens/sec available to our routes when running pinned model variants
- Burst allowance: up to 18,000 tokens/sec for short windows (burst bucket behavior)
- SLO/credit request: service credits if sustained throughput falls below baseline for >30 minutes in any 24h window

I attached our Q1 usage report so you can see the pattern. We’re fine with a staged rollout, but need clear guardrails (latency expectations, throttling behavior, and billing for burst usage). Also want to confirm lead time to provision the extra GPUs once we sign.

Can you propose SLO language we can present internally and share a draft addendum we can review with procurement? Gabe from Healthlytics (cc) will help on the procurement cadence.

Best,
Olivia Barnes
Head of Platform
Synthara Health

Attachment: usage_report_q1_2027.csv (csv, 120KB)

Hi Olivia — thanks for the detail and the report, very helpful.

We can absolutely support a committed baseline TPS and a bounded burst policy. I’ve attached an initial addendum draft that lays out:

- Committed throughput: 12,000 tokens/sec minimum per reserved pool, measured as sustained aggregate over 5-minute windows
- Burst mechanics: token-bucket style burst pool up to 18,000 tokens/sec sustained for up to 10 minutes per hour, with automatic smoothing beyond that
- SLO: 99.5% of 5-minute windows per billing month meeting or exceeding baseline throughput; credit ladder starting at 2% monthly credit for first threshold breach, scaling up thereafter
- Canary & rollout: we propose a 7-day canary at +2 GPUs to validate traffic shaping, then full provisioning of 6 GPUs within 10 business days after signature

Next steps I propose:
1) Quick internal alignment on legal language (I’ve cc’d Marissa to own redlines)
2) Share redlined addendum back to you by EOD next Tue
3) Target DocuSign after procurement approves

I’ll also include a short appendix that explains the burst-handling behavior and how we meter burst charges so there are no surprises.

Attachment: initial-tps-addendum-draft.pdf (pdf, 58KB)

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 29 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: INTERNAL: Synthara renewal — SLO wording and credit ladder proposal

Marissa / Vivek,

Quick internal: Olivia’s team wants the 12k baseline + 18k burst. Procurement will push hard on both guaranteed throughput and on not being charged aggressively for occasional bursts. Proposed negotiation posture below — keep it tight and opinionated:

- Measurables: define baseline as aggregate pool throughput measured across all nodes in the reserved pool, rolling 300s window (5-minute). This avoids spiky miscounts.
- SLO: 99.5% of 5-min windows in a calendar month must meet >=12k TPS. Exclusion: documented maintenance windows and scheduled capacity migrations.
- Latency expectation: P95 per-token generation latency threshold of 320ms for the pinned model under baseline load; if latency rises above this while throughput is still met, we will treat as performance degradation but not SLO breach unless throughput is impacted.
- Credits: three-tier credit ladder: 2% of monthly invoice for single-day breach (>30 continuous min), 8% for multi-day breach (>6 hours cumulative in month), 20% for catastrophic sustained shortfall (>72 hrs). Cap total credits at the monthly commitment.
- Burst: token-bucket with a rolling burst bucket sized at 15% of committed monthly tokens; free bursts up to 18k TPS limited to 10 mins per hour. Beyond that, excess burst consumption billed at discounted overage rate (suggest 40% off list).
- Fallback: automatic model variant fallback to a compatible quantized variant for >15 minutes sustained overload, with transparent routing policy and pre-agreed acceptable degradation profile.

We should also include a clause for a 60-day trial on burst allowance for the first month post-provisioning — if they accept, give a one-time waiver on burst charges and validate measurement. Procurement loves time-limited trials.

If you approve, I’ll fold this into the addendum redline and ask Legal to prep Appendix B (Throughput & Burst Policy).

Thanks,
Karthik

Thanks Karthik — the draft looks solid. A few clarifications/proposals from our side before we ask procurement to sign: 

- Burst trial: we’d like the 60-day burst trial you proposed, but ask that any burst charges in that period be waived and instead tracked for operational review. If we observe abuse, we’ll accept conventional overage billing thereafter.
- Credits: can you cap cumulative monthly credits at 30% of the monthly committed invoice? Also want the first-tier credit to trigger on >15 continuous minutes below baseline (not 30) — that aligns with our customer SLAs.
- Price ask: because we are adding 6 GPUs, request a 25% discount on the per-GPU list rate for the first 12 months of the expanded capacity (we can revert to standard pricing thereafter).

We can agree to the fallback model variant as long as Redwood provides a clear degradation matrix (acceptable output differences) and notification windows prior to automatic fallback.

If you can update the addendum with these items we’ll route to procurement this week.

Best,
Olivia

Subject: Finalizing addendum — next steps & provisioning timeline

Olivia — thanks for the feedback and the clear asks. Summary of agreed positions from Redwood side (for addendum redline):

1) Throughput guarantees
- Committed baseline: 12,000 tokens/sec measured as the rolling 5-minute aggregate across the reserved pool.
- SLO: 99.5% of 5-minute windows per calendar month meeting baseline. Exclusions: scheduled maintenance, agreed migrations, and force majeure.

2) Burst handling and trial
- Burst ceiling: 18,000 tokens/sec. We’ll run a 60-day burst trial starting on provisioning during which burst charges will be waived and burst usage will be tracked for operational review.
- Free burst windows: up to 10 minutes per hour at up to 18k TPS. Excess burst beyond those windows will be billed at a discounted overage rate (40% off list) after the 60-day trial period.

3) Credits and caps
- Credit ladder as discussed (2% / 8% / 20% tiers) with cumulative monthly credits capped at 30% of the monthly committed invoice (per your ask).
- We will adjust the first-tier trigger to >15 continuous minutes below baseline.

4) Pricing
- We can offer a one-time promotional 20% discount on the per-GPU rate for the first 12 months for the 6 additional GPUs (we cannot go to 25% on list pricing, 20% is our approved promotional max for this motion).

5) Fallback behavior
- Automatic fallback to a pre-approved quantized/compatible variant after sustained overload of 15 minutes. Redwood will provide a degradation matrix and 15-minute notification window before automatic fallback is enabled in the production route.

6) Provisioning & rollout
- Target provisioning: 10 business days after executed DocuSign.
- Canary: 7-day live canary on +2 GPUs to validate routing and traffic shaping.
- Full rollout: target May 27, 2027 (contingent on signature and provisioning schedule).

Next steps: I’ll drop a redlined addendum into DocuSign for signatures (link below). Please review the summary and confirm — once signed we’ll start provisioning and CS will run the canary with you.

DocuSign: https://www.docusign.com/sign/placeholder-id

Thanks — looking forward to getting you provisioned.
